sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Peasant Stratification**: The rural society was not monolithic; it was divided into **Khud-kasht** (resident cultivators) and **Pahi-kasht** (non-resident/migrant cultivators).
• **The Village Community**: The **Gaon** or **Mauza** was the basic unit, governed by the **Panchayat** and the **Muqaddam/Patwari**.
• **The Zamindar Class**: A hereditary landed aristocracy holding **Nankar** or **Milkiyat** rights, acting as the primary link between the state and the peasantry.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **'Agrarian Crisis'** theory (Irfan Habib) posits that excessive revenue demand led to peasant flight and the eventual decline of the empire.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Revenue Collection**: The **Zabt** system ensured standardized measurement and cash-based taxation.
• **Social Control**: The **Panchayat** acted as a local judicial body, settling disputes and managing village resources.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: High revenue demand (often 1/3rd to 1/2 of produce) led to rural indebtedness and peasant desertion.
• **Solutions**: Introduction of **Taccavi** (agricultural loans) to encourage cultivation in distressed areas.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'K-P-Z' (Khud, Pahi, Zamindar).
• **Decoded Meaning**: K (Khud-kasht: Resident/Stable), P (Pahi-kasht: Migrant/Mobile), Z (Zamindar: Intermediary/Elite).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Khud-kasht' with 'Zamindar'. Remember: Khud-kasht are peasants (cultivators), while Zamindars are intermediaries (collectors/landlords).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Agrarian Crisis' to link the decline of the Mughal Empire with the socio-economic pressures on the rural peasantry.

keyTakeaways: Mughal rural society was highly stratified based on land rights and mobility.
The Zamindar class was a double-edged sword: essential for revenue collection but a source of local political friction.
The 'Agrarian Crisis' theory remains the most significant analytical framework for explaining the decline of the Mughal state.
